messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: p99 latency breach for customer solis-pay on prod-hosting-us-east. SLO p99 > 2.5s threshold. Alerting oncall. :rotating_light:
Alex (oncall): seeing a bunch of streaming stalls flagged in the dashboard. Vendors show heavy concurrent sessions from a single API key. Confirmed impact to user-facing streams.
Jules (cs): Solis Pay reports checkout widgets stalling for ~10% of requests, customers seeing partial responses. They're on Dedicated pool id:d-7f3.
Alex (oncall): Priya, can you grab heap of metrics? p95/p99 numbers and any queue growth?
Priya (eng-sre): grabbing. Initial check: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.9s on their pool. Streaming stall rate up ~8% last 7m. Request rate up x2 for that key.
Marco (runtime): any unusual prompt shapes? long prefixes or lots of function calls? That changes KV cache profile.
Jules (cs): customer says they rolled a large feature today that fanouts to 10 sub-requests per user action. Might be correlated.
Sam (infra): I'll check node capacity and GPU busy.
Alex (oncall): quick mitigations: 1) scale solis-pay's dedicated pool by +20% if spare capacity, 2) enable short TTL prefix cache, 3) ask customer to rate-limit while we triage.
Priya (eng-sre): telemetry dump: 
```
metric: redwood.inference.latency.p99{pool="d-7f3"} = 2.92
metric: redwood.inference.streaming.stalls{pool="d-7f3"} = 0.082
metric: redwood.inference.kvcache.hit_rate{pool="d-7f3"} dropped from 0.81 -> 0.4 in last 10m
```

Priya (eng-sre): KV cache hit rate tanked — suspect prompt fanout creating many unique prefixes. KV eviction thrash visible.
Marco (runtime): that explains stalls: each new prefix hits cold path + synchronous disk/remote K/V lookup under load -> blocks. We can enable aggressive local prefix caching for that pool as emergency.
Sam (infra): free capacity exists in us-east spare-reserve-2. Will spin up 4 nodes to the dedicated pool. Kicking now.
Alex (oncall): Jules, please ask Solis Pay to temporarily reduce concurrency per session to 4 from 10 if possible. Can they do that?
Jules (cs): pinged account team, they acknowledged and will throttle for the next 20m, rolling out a server-side knob.
Priya (eng-sre): scaled policy applied: autoscale +4 nodes. Watching effects.
Marco (runtime): applying emergency config to enable local prefix cache (ttl=5m, max_entries=100k) for pool d-7f3. This will increase memory but reduce remote lookups.
Alex (oncall): runbook step: if p99 doesn't drop within 5m after the config and scale, route traffic to fallback model (smaller-latency variant) for non-critical endpoints. Marcos — can we do model fallback gracefully?
Marco (runtime): yes, rollout policy available. I'll prepare a canary that maps /v1/generate -> model:redwood-small for 20% of requests from that pool.
Priya (eng-sre): note: logs show gRPC stream window stalls with backpressure increments. Sample log: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:07:21Z] stream_id=abc123 stall_ms=1800 backpressure=1.2 queue_len=37
[2026-03-15T14:07:23Z] stream_id=def456 stall_ms=2300 kvcache_miss=1
```

Nina (prod-mgmt): customer SLA? This is impacting live checkouts, we should prioritize mitigation over cost.
Alex (oncall): agree. Prioritize availability. Sam/Marco/Priya coordinate.
Sam (infra): nodes joined, pool slots +4. New capacity online: nodex8->nodex12.
Priya (eng-sre): after scale + cache flip, p99 dropped to 1.1s within 4 minutes. Streaming stalls fell to ~2%.
Jules (cs): Solis Pay confirms reduced user-visible stalls but still seeing occasional partial responses during checkout on large carts. They pushed a delayed retry on client side.
Marco (runtime): follow-up: we need a longer-term fix: recommend prefix dedup on client (batching sub-requests), and model-side batching improvements. Also propose adding a routing policy that shards high-fanout keys across multiple pools to reduce KV hotspot.
Alex (oncall): immediate action log: 
- scaled dedicated pool +4 nodes (Sam)
- enabled local prefix cache ttl=5m (Marco)
- advised customer throttle to 4 conc (Jules)
- prepared canary fallback to smaller model at 20% (Marco, ready but not flipped)
- monitoring p99 and stall metrics (Priya)

Priya (eng-sre): metrics now: 
```
redwood.inference.latency.p99{pool="d-7f3"} = 1.12
redwood.inference.streaming.stalls{pool="d-7f3"} = 0.021
redwood.inference.kvcache.hit_rate{pool="d-7f3"} = 0.78
```

Alex (oncall): marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll keep the emergency cache config for 24h and schedule a postmortem.
Jules (cs): customer asked for timeline on root cause and permanent mitigations. I'll draft comms: explain fanout + prefix churn, immediate mitigations, and propose next steps (client batching + routing policy).
Nina (prod-mgmt): schedule postmortem + action items with runtime and SRE. Priority: 1) add sharded routing for high-fanout API keys, 2) detect sudden fanout pattern and auto-throttle/fallback, 3) client guidance for prefix reuse.
Marco (runtime): noted. I'll capture config diff and perf numbers in the runbook entry.
Priya (eng-sre): reopening monitoring alert to auto-escalate if p99 > 1.5s for more than 3m.
Alex (oncall): thanks team. Keeping thread pinned until postmortem created. :white_check_mark:
